title: BASIC BODY PARTS OF DAIRY CATTLE

facts: The module section is titled 'BASIC BODY PARTS OF DAIRY CATTLE'.
Objective 1 of this module is to familiarize the basic parts of a dairy cow.
Objective 2 of this module is to learn the digestive physiology of dairy cow.
The paralumbar fossa is represented by a triangular depression area on the flank/lumbar region of the cow.
The loin refers to the dorsal region along the top of the cow bordered anteriorly toward the shoulder and posteriorly near the hip.
The crest and poll are located dorsally near the head and neck; the poll is situated at the top of the head.
The anterior facial features labeled include the forehead and the muzzle.
The lower neck and chest parts include the dewlap, brisket, and elbow.
The front leg anatomy includes the knee and hoof.
The circumference measurement around the chest just behind the front legs is indicated as the heart girth.
The hindquarters include the hook (tuber coxae), pin (tuber ischii), and tail head.
The tail ends with the tuft of hair known as the switch.
The hind leg joints and structures labeled include the stifle, hock, dewclaw, heel, and hoof.
The mammary system labeled on the cow consists of the udder and teat.
